title: Turn with the gyro
summary: Turn exactly 90 degrees by watching the yaw angle.
what: The robot turns right 90 degrees four times, using a My Block called TurnRight.
why: The hub has a gyro sensor that measures how far the robot has turned (the yaw angle). Turning "180 wheel degrees" can be off if a wheel slips, but turning until the gyro says 90 checks the real turn. Turning right makes the yaw go up, turning left makes it go down.
try: Make a TurnLeft block: spin with -20 and 20 and wait until yaw is less than the minus target.
Try a faster turn speed. Do you need to stop earlier?
Use TurnRight inside the square program instead of the steering turn.
